expected_evidence: Cosmogenic isotope excursions (14C, 10Be, 36Cl) in ice cores and varved sediments precisely dated to ~10,950 BP that would be diagnostic of a gamma-ray/cosmic ionization event (their absence or mistiming is the key refutational evidence)

Absence or mismatch of impact-proxy markers (platinum spike, nanodiamonds, iridium anomaly, magnetic spherules) with any gamma-ray-burst-specific signature, distinguishing this mechanism from a conventional impactor
Astronomical/astrophysical case for a candidate nearby supernova or gamma-ray-burst source (or lack thereof) capable of irradiating Earth at that date
Faunal chronology (radiocarbon-dated megafaunal remains) showing extinction pulse timing inconsistent with a single sharp ionization event, i.e., extinctions staggered/gradual rather than synchronous
Ancient DNA / population genetic data on North American megafauna showing decline patterns (bottleneck timing, genetic diversity loss) inconsistent with an acute radiation-driven mass mortality

Ozone-depletion or biological stress proxies (e.g., UV-B damage markers in preserved spores/pollen, unusual mutation load) that a gamma-ray ionization event would be expected to leave, and their presence/absence
Model-prior literature record of the gamma-ray-burst-as-YD-trigger hypothesis (e.g., Melott & Thomas-type proposals) and subsequent critique/refutation in the scientific literature
response.rationale: This hypothesis concerns a refutation of a specific mechanistic claim (gamma-ray ionization from a cosmic event) as the cause of North American megafaunal extinction, dated to the Younger Dryas boundary (~10,950 BP). The most diagnostic evidence classes are geological (ice-core/sediment isotope and impact-proxy records) and astronomical (cosmogenic isotope excursions, candidate source identification), which have relatively good preservation and detection potential for this period (younger-dryas row: geological 0.65, astronomical 0.7). Genetic (ancient DNA of megafauna, 0.3) and material/archaeological faunal chronology (0.35) evidence is moderately preserved and has been actively studied. Textual (0.0) and linguistic (0.05) evidence are irrelevant/non-existent for a pre-literate period and should not count against the hypothesis. Oral tradition (0.1) and iconographic (0.1) evidence are essentially unavailable this far back. Model-prior literature (0.3) exists as a real scientific debate (a gamma-ray-burst/supernova trigger for the Younger Dryas radiocarbon spike has been proposed and contested in the literature — flagged here as model-prior, not verified from the evidence text). Weighting toward the geological/astronomical/genetic channels most relevant to testing an ionization mechanism, and down-weighting textual/linguistic/oral/iconographic channels that are structurally near-zero for this period, yields a composite detectability of roughly 0.45. Given this, an absence of a clean, dated cosmogenic isotope spike or corroborating astrophysical source is a plausible and expected form of 'evidence of refutation' rather than an indication that the underlying question is unanswerable — the refutation is plausible and detectable within the surviving proxy record, so falsity (of the gamma-ray-impact-as-cause claim) can be reasonably distinguished from mere non-detection.
